background.title: Entropic quantum error correction for independent and correlated amplitude damping errors
background.abstract: The idea of using quantum entropy for quantum error correction (QEC) has existed for a long time. However, its computational complexity has limited its practical use: even a $[[4,1]]$ code for standard independent amplitude damping errors involves a $256\times 256$ Hermitian matrix, so the approach scales poorly as the codeword length increases. For correlated errors, the situation is even worse. In this paper, we show that, by using the insights developed in our previous paper and exploiting certain structures of quantum conditional mutual information, we can solve these problems exactly by hand, using only $2\times 2$ unitary matrices. By examining the entropy, we identify the leakage channels and the amount of leakage exactly, then define the recovery map accordingly. The rules defining our recovery map are simple, intuitive, and computationally inexpensive: for independent errors, it is based on 16 explicitly given orthonormal vectors and 6 instructions; for correlated errors, it is based on 6 explicitly given orthonormal vectors and 6 instructions. Our method sacrifices little in terms of performance: for the widely used entanglement fidelity, our simple QEC recovery map achieves a sharp result; for the worst-case fidelity, the best result is about $9\%$ better than ours; for correlated errors, there are no comparable results for short codewords. Among the known techniques, our recovery map is the first non-global one. The calculations use elementary linear algebra and calculus, and is presented in great detail.

background.title: Next-to-Next-to-Next-to-Leading-Order Prediction for the Radiative $B_{u}^- \to γ\ell^{-} \bar ν_{\ell}$ Decay
background.abstract: We accomplish for the first time the three-loop computation of the photonic radiative jet function in soft-collinear effective theory, which constitutes the last missing and most difficult ingredient for the complete next-to-next-to-next-to-leading-order QCD prediction of the simplest radiative $B_{u}^- \to γ\ell^{-} \bar ν_{\ell}$ decay with an energetic photon at leading power. Importantly, the most prominent three-loop contribution to the radiative bottom-meson decay form factors turns out to arise from the newly determined QCD correction to the jet function rather than from the recently obtained hard correction. We further demonstrate explicitly that our full three-loop calculation of these non-hadronic radiative $B$-meson decay form factors appear to be highly beneficial for an improved extraction of the fundamental shape parameter $λ_B$ of the leading-twist $B$-meson light-cone distribution amplitude.

background.title: Rigidity for pivotal braided r-categories of moderate growth and applications to vertex operator algebras
background.abstract: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be an abelian pivotal braided r-category with simple unit object $\mathbf{1}$ over any field. We present a ChatGPT-generated proof, prompted by Bin Gui, that any object $X$ in $\mathcal{C}$ of moderate growth, in the sense that $\dim\mathrm{End}(X^{\otimes n})<n!$ for some $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$, is rigid. The proof crucially uses ideas from the recent proof of Etingof and Penneys that $X$ is rigid if it is also non-negligible, that is, $X\otimes Y$ contains $\mathbf{1}$ as a direct summand for some object $Y$. In the present paper, the non-negligible assumption is removed using a rigidity criterion developed previously by the author for use in non-semisimple categories. We also present a variant result (found without further AI assistance) that $X$ is also rigid if $\dim\mathrm{Hom}((DX)^{\otimes n}\otimes X^{\otimes n},\mathbf{1})<n!$ for some $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$, where $D$ is the Grothendieck-Verdier duality functor of $\mathcal{C}$. Using this variant, we show that if $V$ is a simple self-contragredient vertex operator algebra such that the category $\mathcal{C}^1_V$ of $C_1$-cofinite grading-restricted generalized $V$-modules is closed under contragredient modules, then $\mathcal{C}^1_V$ is a locally finite $\mathbb{C}$-linear abelian rigid braided ribbon category. We also show that if $V$ is a simple $\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$-graded self-contragredient $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra, then the category of all grading-restricted generalized $V$-modules is a (not necessarily semisimple) modular tensor category.

background.title: Observation of Non-Equilibrium Phonon Loss Across a Solid-Superfluid Interface
background.abstract: We measure the performance of an athermal phonon calorimeter in vacuum and in thermal contact with superfluid $^4$He. Using a cryogenic photon calibration system, we show that the superfluid suppresses the collection of the phonon signal by over 99\%. We conclude that submerged sensors will not benefit TESSERACT's superfluid helium dark matter target, but that superfluid helium may be useful to superconducting qubits as a sink for athermal phonons generated by radiation and other spontaneous sources. Our measurement is the first probe of solid-to-superfluid phonon transmission at energies higher than those stably supportable by the superfluid. We discuss thermal flow inside the calorimeter, as well as systematics from an alternative calibration scheme.

background.title: Rigidity of the moving particle lemma for the interchange process
background.abstract: Let $G=(V,c)$ be a finite connected weighted graph. We establish the exact conditions for attaining equality in the moving particle lemma for the interchange process on $G$ subject to a unit voltage drop across two terminal vertices $x\neq y \in V$. First, equality can occur only in irreducible representations indexed by partitions with at most two rows. We then show that the equality phenomenon beyond the constant and linear sectors is already visible in the two-particle exclusion process. Such equality occurs in exactly two cases: either the harmonic $x$--$y$ voltage is $\frac12$ on every nonterminal vertex, and the induced nonterminal graph $G[V\setminus\{x,y\}]$ is disconnected; or the harmonic voltage is constant on each connected component of $G[V\setminus \{x,y\}]$, and both voltage values $a$ and $1-a$, with $0\le a<\frac12$, occur. In each case we compute the equality kernel in every degree and particle sector. The resulting decomposition gives the complete equality kernel for exclusion and, through the regular representation, for the interchange process.

background.title: Localization for Lipschitz monotone quasi-periodic operators with power-law hopping
background.abstract: We prove spectral and dynamical localization for quasi-periodic operators on $\mathbb Z^d$ with Lipschitz monotone potentials and power-law hopping. For sufficiently small coupling, localization holds at every allowed phase whenever the hopping decay exponent $r$ exceeds the Diophantine exponent $τ$. The proof is based on multiscale analysis with exponentially growing scales. We use homotopy in the coupling constant to select the local eigenvalue branches and Schur complement estimates to control the successive elimination of coordinates.

background.title: Classical weak antilocalization in electron hydrodynamics
background.abstract: Weak localization is strongly suppressed in electron hydrodynamics, where frequent electron--electron collisions rapidly dephase the Cooperon. Nevertheless, disorder can still produce a logarithmic correction to the bare hydrodynamic resistivity. We show that spatial fluctuations of the momentum-relaxation rate generate a classical memory kernel through the diffusive return of transverse momentum. In two dimensions, this return is logarithmic, as in weak localization, but involves a single shear propagator rather than quantum interference. Conservation laws and positivity of dissipation fix its antilocalizing sign: the return reduces momentum relaxation and hence the bulk resistivity. Unlike quantum weak localization, the logarithm is cut off by momentum relaxation and has a viscosity-dependent amplitude. For temperature-independent impurity friction, the resistivity correction scales as $-T^2\ln(T_ξ/T)$ in a Fermi liquid and $-T\ln(T_ξ/T)$ in a Planckian metal. In channels, the return competes with viscosity renormalization, and a width scan separates the two effects.

background.title: Quantum Fundamental Groups of Spaces with Finite-Sheeted Universal Covers
background.abstract: Discrete quantum groups have attracted much interest, but there was a lack of natural examples until Voigt constructed quantum permutations of finite and infinite sets in arXiv:2208.01310. In this paper, we construct the quantum fundamental groups that contain the classical fundamental groups as subgroups. This is a new class of natural examples of discrete quantum groups arising from symmetries of covering spaces in topology. We characterize quantum fundamental groups for a wide class of examples, including $\mathbb{RP}^2$. We show that these quantum fundamental groups are genuinely quantum for spaces with finite fundamental groups that are either non-abelian or of non prime order.

background.title: Spatial scaling of heterogeneity transfer from boron concentration to absorbed dose in boron neutron capture therapy
background.abstract: We investigate how the amplitude and spatial correlation length of boron-concentration fluctuations affect the boron-induced absorbed-dose distribution in boron neutron capture therapy (BNCT). The spatial energy-deposition response of alpha particles and lithium nuclei is obtained using Geant4 and convolved with three-dimensional correlated lognormal boron fields under a uniform neutron field. Approximately $90\%$ of the reaction-product energy is deposited within a radius of $6.00~μ\mathrm{m}$, with a characteristic deposition length of $\ell_B\approx2.05~μ\mathrm{m}$. Dose heterogeneity increases with both the fluctuation amplitude $H$ and correlation length $ξ$, while the transfer factor $S=CV_D/H$ exhibits an approximate scaling collapse as a function of $ξ/\ell_B$. Analytical Gaussian and lognormal--Gaussian models provide reference predictions for this behavior. At short correlation lengths, the Geant4 response yields a higher transfer factor than a Gaussian response with the same characteristic length, highlighting the influence of the energy-deposition shape on dose smoothing. For $D_{95}$, defined as the dose received by at least $95\%$ of the modeled volume, the relative difference between homogeneous and heterogeneous boron-dose models reaches $(86.62\pm1.07)\%$ at $H=1.2$ and a target ratio $ξ/\ell_B=6$. We show that mean boron concentration alone is insufficient to characterize spatial nonuniformity of the boron-dose component.

background.title: Exoplanets are predominately aligned with exo-Kuiper Belts
background.abstract: The architectures of planetary systems encode their formation and dynamical histories. In the Solar System, the near alignment of planetary orbits, the Kuiper Belt, and the Sun's equator supports planet formation in a rotating disk of gas and dust. However, some exoplanet systems show planets on orbits misaligned with their host stars or other planets, raising the question of whether misalignments are primordial or produced by post-formation dynamics. We present the first population-level constraints on the mutual inclinations of 32 planets in 16 systems relative to debris disks. We find that planets across orbital distances from 0.1 to 100 AU are predominantly aligned with the debris disks within 10 deg (30/32 planets). The alignment holds across systems spanning tens of million years to a few gigayears in age. These results indicate that the aligned architecture of the Solar System is representative of the birth conditions of exoplanet systems.

background.title: Painlevé quadrics and their confluence for the dispersionless Kadomtsev-Petviashvili equation
background.abstract: We construct and study a distinguished class of solutions of the dispersionless Kadomtsev--Petviashvili (dKP) equation whose geometry is governed by the first and second Painlevé equations. The level surfaces of these solutions correspond to three geometric families of central quadrics, and we determine when their level surfaces degenerate into planes. In the parabolic family parametrised by $\mathrm{P_I}$, degenerate levels occur at the stationary points of the transcendent. For the hyperbolic family parametrised by rational solutions of $\mathrm{P_{II}}$, we show that degenerate levels occur at points where consecutive solutions intersect and we give a precise count of such degeneracies. In the homogeneous elliptic family, the Hastings--McLeod solution of $\mathrm{P_{II}}$ is characterised, up to sign, as the unique non-trivial real pole-free solution with Airy asymptotics whose quadric has no finite degenerate level. Finally, under critical scaling, the quadrics generated by the $n$-th rational Painlevé-II solution converge locally, and away from poles, to the parabolic quadrics associated with the Painlevé-I tritronquée solution, with error $O(n^{-1/5})$.

background.title: Hidden Quantum Markov Processes: Mealy Formulation and Observable Reduction
background.abstract: We formulate hidden quantum Markov processes in a Mealy architecture using a single completely positive unital transition expectation coupling the present hidden system, the emitted output, and the next hidden system. Together with a boundary state, it generates a quasi-local, finitely correlated hidden--output state; for the commutative generator associated with a classical Mealy kernel, this state is the full joint law of the classical Mealy model. Moore realizations correspond to transition expectations that factor on the prescribed hidden algebra. We establish a rank obstruction to such factorization and prove its sufficiency for isometric generators: factorization holds exactly when the induced hidden-memory channel has Kraus rank at most the hidden Hilbert-space dimension. The Kraus rank also gives the minimal intermediate Hilbert-space dimension. When the hidden and output dimensions are at least two, the factorizable isometric generators form a closed subset of measure zero. For any fixed projective readout, a Mealy generator induces an operational hidden quantum Markov model in the sense of Monràs, Beige and Wiesner; conversely, every finite-dimensional operational model admits a Mealy lift on the same memory space with a rank-one readout. For their cluster-state instrument, two isometric, Moore-factorizable lifts with the same instrument and initial memory state yield identical measured output statistics but different quantum output states: one has marginals entangled across $1|2\cdots n$ for $n\geq3$, with three-output negativity $\tfrac12$, whereas the other has fully separable marginals. Thus operational equivalence does not determine output entanglement.

background.title: Link invariants in nilpotent group gauge theories
background.abstract: We consider 3-dimensional topological gauge theories with nilpotent gauge groups, both finite, that is Dijkgraaf-Witten theories, and continuous, that is Chern-Simons theories. Abelian topological quantum field theories are exactly those which do not detect the Borromean rings, and nilpotent gauge groups provide the natural next steps beyond the abelian case. We show that the untwisted Dijkgraaf-Witten theory with gauge group $G$ detects Brunnian links with up to $n+1$ components, but no Brunnian links with more components, if and only if $G$ is $n$-step nilpotent. Moreover, the expectation values of such links are determined by their Milnor invariants. We also study the properties of Chern-Simons theories with nilpotent Lie groups and draw parallels with those of the Dijkgraaf-Witten theories. Finally, we conjecture, using the Lazard correspondence, a relation between expectation values of line operators in the two types of theories, and test it in examples.

background.title: Internal diameter bounds for DLA on random planar maps under invariance principles
background.abstract: We establish sublinear bounds for the internal diameter of External Diffusion Limited Aggregation (DLA) clusters on random planar maps. We develop two conditional DLA growth results for deterministic planar maps: the weaker condition yielding sublinear growth for DLA, and the stronger yielding polynomially sublinear growth for DLA. We then verify the strong assumption a.s. for the $γ$-mated CRT maps, and the weak condition a.s. for ergodic scale-free random environments, establishing the corresponding a.s bounds.

background.title: Exponential Lower Bounds for the Spherically Averaged Density of Atoms
background.abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of the spherically averaged density $\widetilde ρ$ for fermionic bound states of the $N$-electron atomic Hamiltonian $H_{N,Z}$ with nuclear charge $Z$. For the density associated with an eigenfunction satisfying $H_{N,Z}ψ=Eψ$, we show that if the energy $E$ is below the bottom of the essential spectrum $Σ:=\inf\mathop{\rm ess.spec} (H_{N,Z})$, then \[ \lim_{r\to\infty}\frac{\ln \widetilde ρ(r)}{r} =\lim_{r\to\infty}\frac{d}{dr}{\ln \widetildeρ(r)} =-2α_0, \] with $α_0=\sup\{α\ge 0\colon e^{2αr}\widetilde ρ\in L^1(\mathbb{R_+},r^2dr)\}$. The same is true at threshold in certain cases. Moreover, we prove $α_0^2=Σ-E$ for the ground states of $H_{3,Z}$ with sufficiently large $Z$.

background.title: Essential spectrum of singularly perturbed Dirac operators on bounded domains
background.abstract: In this paper self-adjoint Dirac operators on bounded domains in $\mathbb{R}^2$ and $\mathbb{R}^3$ with elliptic boundary conditions perturbed by singular $δ$-shell potentials supported on compact curves or surfaces are considered. While the unperturbed operator has purely discrete spectrum, it is shown that certain critical values of the interaction strengths lead to the appearance of essential spectrum. More precisely, each connected component of the interaction support, where the coupling constants have such critical values, produces in dimension two a point and in dimension three even a closed interval in the essential spectrum, where the size of the latter depends on the geometry and the coupling constants.

background.title: Magnetic kink instability of jet-wind outflows. I. Static column configuration
background.abstract: We describe the results of computer simulations investigating the stability of an axisymmetric static equilibrium combining a highly magnetised ($σ=10^3$) central column and a mildly ($σ=0.1$) to weakly ($σ=0.001$) magnetised outer shell with a helical and mostly force-free magnetic field of constant pitch. The measured linear growth rates of the instability are in agreement with the maximum growth rate for a uniform density column with a force-free magnetic field of constant pitch obtained by Appl et al. (2000), being only a little bit higher. At the non-linear phase, the interface separating the central column and the outer shell develops the characteristic corkscrew shape, with the space inside and between the coils of the corkscrew filled by the shell plasma. In high-resolution runs, a secondary instability is seen as well. It has the form of helical protuberances of low-$σ$ plasma intruding inside the corkscrew coils. These appear to be aligned with the local magnetic field lines. We tentatively identify the secondary instability as the magnetic Rayleigh-Taylor instability. Overall, the results indicate that the current-driven kink instability may provide the baryon-loading of AGN jets suggested by the observations.

background.title: Restoring Consistency with Poynting's Theorem in Numerical MHD and RMHD
background.abstract: For perfectly conducting plasmas, Poynting's theorem states that the time rate of change of electromagnetic energy density equals the negative of the divergence of the Poynting flux. To the best of our knowledge, this involutive theorem has never been mimetically incorporated in codes. We show that there is an inconsistency in MHD and RMHD codes that evolve face-centered magnetic fields in globally-divergence-free fashion. This is because the face-centered flux of energy density, which incorporates a Poynting vector, is evaluated using one-dimensional Riemann solvers that are applied at face-centers. However, the face-centered magnetic fields are evolved according to edge-centered electric fields that come from two-dimensional Riemann solvers that are applied to the edges of a zone. While edge-centered electric fields are used to evolve the magnetic field, they have no influence on the face-centered Poynting flux. For situations where the magnetic energy is much larger than the thermal energy, this causes a negative pressure to be evaluated at the zone-centers. This paper restores consistency by using edge-centered variables to evaluate a face-centered Poynting flux. A simple accuracy-preserving correction is made to the face-centered flux of energy density. We show that it helps considerably in simulations that have very strong magnetic fields.

background.title: Maxwell's equations with thin wires in critical scaling
background.abstract: We derive effective equations for a situation in which electromagnetic waves hit an array of very thin wires. We study two cases, perfectly conducting wires and highly conducting wires, and investigate in both the critical scaling of the parameters. The electric field $E^η$ and the magnetic field $H^η$ satisfy the time-harmonic Maxwell equations, and the small parameter $η>0$ is the spacing of the wires. A non-critical scaling of the wires implies either that the wires have no effect or that the tangential component of the limiting electric field in the direction of the wires vanishes along the effective interface. In the critical scaling, we observe an interesting effect: The wires act as oscillators and there is a relation between the electric field in longitudinal direction and the jump of the magnetic field in transversal direction involving second derivatives of a flux quantity.

background.title: A Double Sided LGAD-Based Detector Providing Timing, Position, and Track Angle Information
background.abstract: We describe a detector concept which combines small pixels enabled by 3D sensor-electronics integration with gain produced by a Low Gain Avalanche Diode (LGAD) layer. The detector is double-sided, with electrons collected by the cathode, which provides timing information, and an anode with small pixels to provide position and angle information. The cathode can be coarse grained, providing timing with fewer fast amplifiers to limit power consumption. The anode layer benefits from the gain of the LGAD, with larger signals that also limit the power needed. Position can be reconstructed by measuring the pattern of total charge deposited on the anode. Angle and depth of charge deposit can be measured by the shapes of the anode pulses. We describe a possible assembly technology based on 3D integration.

background.title: Quantum Preparation without Disturbance: Information Costs and Hypothesis Testing
background.abstract: We determine the minimum information cost of preparing either of two quantum states with one common device while preserving its memory. Measured by the Umegaki relative entropy between the two possible memory states, this minimum is the Belavkin-Staszewski relative entropy of the target states. If the memory may instead be consumed, the minimum is their Umegaki relative entropy. More generally, for any divergence satisfying data processing, memory preservation selects the maximal extension of its classical restriction. We also study the cost of requiring only finitely many outputs, with the costs increasing from Umegaki to Belavkin-Staszewski relative entropy as the number of outputs grows. Finally, we consider hypothesis testing of an unknown device over independent runs. The optimal Stein exponent per run converges to the Belavkin-Staszewski relative entropy whenever the number of outputs per run diverges. This gives an operational characterization of the Belavkin-Staszewski relative entropy in quantum statistics.

background.title: From pure spinor modules to superspace superfields
background.abstract: We relate the pure spinor formalism to the superspace description of constrained superfields and gauge multiplets, mainly for abelian two-dimensional N=(2,2) supersymmetry, with three- and four-dimensional N=1 examples for comparison. For each multiplet we give an explicit module over the supertranslation Chevalley-Eilenberg algebra and match its reconstruction with the known superfields. First-order constraints come from modules supported on linear subspaces of the nilpotence variety, and higher-order ones, such as the complex-linear constraint, from Yoneda products of their Ext classes. Requiring a connection to act on given matter and its conjugate restricts its curvature, which yields the ordinary, twisted and semichiral vector multiplets with their field strengths. The module of each vector multiplet is the fiber product over the origin of the coordinate rings of the matter supports: its potentials are differences of partial potentials, and its gauge parameters are the matter superfields. For the large vector multiplet this fiber product is not a quotient of the pure spinor ring; its field strengths are four odd semichiral superfields, and partial regluing gives its constrained versions.

background.title: Latent resonances in oscillator networks
background.abstract: In networks of coupled oscillators, from neural circuits to power grids, damping is expected to suppress oscillations because of its dissipativity. Here we show that local damping can, counterintuitively, amplify oscillations along some input-output channels, while the network's global oscillation energy decreases and its spectral properties improve. The amplified oscillation arises from a latent resonance that lies in the spectrum yet barely manifests. The added passive damping reshapes this resonance by mixing it with adjacent eigenmodes. In random power-grid networks, damping can boost weakly responding channels by more than an order of magnitude, while subdominant channels can grow to exceed the originally strongest channel. Damping thus not only suppresses oscillations but also provides a way to redistribute oscillatory energy. For any passive network, the amplified response and its upper bound follow exactly from baseline quantities, offering a principled route for network design and control.

background.title: The speed of convergence for propagation of chaos in the mean-field Ising model
background.abstract: We derive sharp relative-entropy asymptotics for increasing propagation of chaos in the Curie--Weiss model at zero external field. For every fixed inverse temperature $0<β<1$, the relative entropy of a $k$-spin marginal with respect to the symmetric product measure is $$ \frac{β^2}{4(1-β)^2}\frac{k(k-1)}{N^2}+o\left(\frac{k^2}{N^2}\right),\qquad k=o(N). $$ At the critical inverse temperature $β=1$, the rate changes to $α_{\mathrm c}^2 k(k-1)/(4N)+o(k^2/N)$ in the regime $k=o(\sqrt N)$, where $α_{\mathrm c}$ is the second moment of the limiting quartic law of the rescaled magnetization. We also obtain asymptotics for sequences $β_N\uparrow1$ that interpolate between these two regimes. Crucially, the proof reveals that the pair correlations determine the leading correction to the likelihood ratio, providing precise control of both the chi-square divergence and relative entropy.

background.title: Density fluctuations in pseudo-streamer and helmet streamer: Generation, propagation and comparison with Metis observations
background.abstract: Recent white-light observations from the Metis coronagraph on board Solar Orbiter have shown the presence of propagating density fluctuations with a period of $\sim5$ minutes, particularly in the observationally bright regions of helmet streamers and pseudo-streamers. These density fluctuations have been shown to originate from magnetohydrodynamic wave modes -- slow and fast modes can directly compress the plasma, whereas Alfvén waves generate density fluctuations via a non-linear coupling with the slow and fast modes. In general, in low plasma $β$ regions, slow modes contribute more towards the generation of density fluctuations, whereas in high $β$ regions, there are significant contributions from both slow and fast waves. In this work, we investigate the propagation of (non-linear) Alfvén waves and the associated density fluctuations using a 2.5D axisymmetric global solar wind model that includes two distinct magnetic field topologies -- a helmet streamer and a pseudo-streamer. Key differences in these magnetic configurations give rise to differences in the wave behaviour due to, for example, the presence of a current sheet in the helmet streamer and an X-type null point in the pseudo-streamer, and the structure of the $β= 1$ layer in both magnetic field configurations. This leads to the possible creation of prominent interference patterns along the helmet streamer axis, which do not appear along the pseudo-streamer axis. Unlike in the streamer region, we also find that along the pseudo-streamer axis, the contribution to the density fluctuations is due to the fast waves only, despite being in a low $β$ plasma.

background.title: A systematic comparison of physics-informed neural networks and mechanistic models for epidemic modeling and forecasting
background.abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have recently been applied to epidemic modeling and forecasting with promising results. These methods integrate mechanistic knowledge with data-driven learning. Yet, their comparative performance against well-established, and simpler epidemic models is underexplored. Here, we conduct a systematic comparison of a PINN-based framework and a stochastic mechanistic model. Both approaches share the same age-structured SEIRD core and rolling-window forecasting pipeline, in a deliberately minimal setting. We evaluate their retrospective fits and probabilistic forecasts in two synthetic scenarios and the first COVID-19 wave in London. Interestingly, while PINNs underperform in synthetic scenarios, they achieve better performance on real data. Furthermore, PINNs provide narrower uncertainty intervals and sharper estimation of parameters in synthetic scenarios. Our findings confirm PINNs as a promising tool in epidemiology. At the same time, the results reaffirm the value of simpler approaches such as traditional compartmental models, and promote additional benchmarking studies.

background.title: BeST: Beta splatted tomography for direct reconstruction from coherent imaging measurements
background.abstract: Conventional coherent X-ray tomography requires the phase of each projection to be reconstructed with high fidelity. However, individual reconstructed projections might be flawed, e.g. due to positioning errors, yielding inconsistent tomographic reconstructions. By directly coupling phase retrieval and tomography, consistency is enforced through a common object volume. But reconstructing a full volume demands substantial computational resources. To reduce this demand, we introduce Beta Splatted Tomography (BeST), which represents the common object volume using compactly supported beta primitives with closed-form analytical projections, enabling efficient reconstruction directly from coherent scattering images. This representation substantially reduces the number of optimizable parameters compared to a voxel grid. We demonstrate BeST on experimental datasets from hard X-ray near-field holography and far-field ptychography measurements. In both cases, the joint technique improves reconstruction quality compared to two-step methods.

background.title: Local Quantum Metrology: Precision Limits for Observers in QFT
background.abstract: How precisely can an observer estimate a parameter related to a quantum field? This question is answered for quantum-mechanical systems using the SLD--Bures--Fisher metric and the quantum Cramér--Rao bound. However, local algebras in relativistic quantum field theory are of type III: they carry no trace and normal states have no density matrices, so the SLD quantum Fisher information and the quantum Cramér--Rao bound cannot be defined in the usual way. We define the SLD (Bures) quantum Fisher information on arbitrary von Neumann algebras through Uhlmann's transition probability and prove a quantum Cramér--Rao bound for collective measurements. We also show that the bound is sharp, and equals the largest classical Fisher information obtainable by measurements in the region.

background.title: Contractions of realizations and differential invariants of the algebra sl(2,C)
background.abstract: In this paper, we formalize a method for constructing limit transitions between local realizations of Lie algebras based on contractions of the corresponding algebras. In the complex holomorphic category, contractions of faithful realizations of the special linear algebra sl(2, C) to the complex three-dimensional Poincaré algebra and the Weyl-Heisenberg algebra are explicitly constructed. For the contraction of a generating realization of the algebra sl(2,C) to the algebra g_{3.4}^{-1}, differential invariants are constructed and a limit system of Newtonian type is found.

background.title: Towards invertibility of derived categories of sheaf-theoretic line operators
background.abstract: We investigate when the braided monoidal $\infty$-categories of sheaf-theoretic line operators of $3$-dimensional topological quantum field theories are invertible in the higher Morita category, so that they determine invertible $4$-dimensional anomaly theories. We consider a zoo of different examples which are inherently derived. First, enhancing Ben-Zvi--Francis--Nadler, we show that a symmetric monoidal category of quasi-coherent sheaves $\mathrm{QC}(X)$ is invertible only if $X$ is a point, and convolution categories on loop stacks are Morita trivial whenever the stack satisfies descent along its diagonal, e.g. for classifying stacks. Secondly, we provide an example showing that, unlike for finite braided tensor categories, non-degeneracy does not imply invertibility in the derived setting: For an odd vector space $V[1]$, the $2$-shifted $\mathcal{D}$-modules $\mathrm{DMod}^2(V[1])$ are $3$-dualizable and non-degenerate but neither factorizable nor cofactorizable. This category is closely related to the line operators of linear Rozansky--Witten theory. Finally, we define an anomaly of a group action on an invertible braided monoidal $\infty$-category as a Witt class over $\mathrm{Rep}(G)$, and show that the category of representations of the quantum group of a torus at a root of unity is invertible relative to its quantum Frobenius.

background.title: Global saddle selection and exact absolute-instability boundaries for convection in porous media with throughflow
background.abstract: In the Darcy-Prats problem, horizontal throughflow leaves the temporal onset of convection unchanged but raises the heating required for a localized disturbance to grow at a fixed point. The saddle equations give five candidates, but only the saddles reached by deformation of the Fourier contour contribute to the growth. For $Ra>π^2$, $Pe>0$ we prove that the same off-axis pair contributes throughout the domain: no Stokes transition can change its contribution. Its growth gives a unique analytic absolute threshold, first reached by the lowest vertical mode. Rescaling transfers the selection to Forchheimer drag, transverse rolls of a power-law fluid, anisotropic permeability, an open upper boundary and a vertical magnetic field. A shift of the same growth function accounts for interphase heat exchange in a model of metallic foam. At prescribed throughflow the threshold increases strictly with either resistance coefficient. In particular, a vertical magnetic field raises the absolute threshold at fixed Péclet number. Tabulated thresholds check the reduction. Algebraic elimination gives the boundary polynomial, and frequency recovery selects its physical branch. At the Darcy level the selected saddles trace an arc of the elliptic curve 11a3, a degeneration of a genus-two family at nonzero shifted levels. Series inversion on this arc gives an integer weak-throughflow series and an all-order strong-throughflow expansion. Rational certificates establish the exact convergence radii of both series on the selected sheets.

background.title: Performance and Stability Studies of GEM Detectors for High Energy Physics Applications
background.abstract: R\&D on different gas-filled detectors such as Gas Electron Multipliers (GEMs), Resistive Plate Chambers (RPCs) and straw tubes has been carried out in the detector laboratory of Bose Institute for more than a decade, keeping in mind present and future high-energy physics experiments. In this article, performance studies of a single-mask triple-GEM detector using a $^{55}$Fe X-ray source with an Ar/CO$_2$ (70/30) gas mixture are described. The study focuses mainly on the gain, energy resolution, count rate, and stability of the chamber under long-term irradiation. The experimental setup, methodology, and analysis results are presented.

background.title: Numerical experiments on sunspot penumbral flows
background.abstract: We present 3D radiative magnetohydrodynamic simulations of sunspots with a self-consistently generated penumbra. We analyze the impact of resolution, surrounding opposite-polarity fields and subsurface large-scale flows on the structure and stability of the simulated penumbra. Extended penumbral filaments are obtained for a subset of the simulations. These were run at 25 km (15 km) horizontal (vertical) resolution and with initial conditions favoring fields with strong horizontal components in the penumbral region. The surface velocities in these simulations are consistent with observations of Evershed flow. The main driving mechanism remains the same as illustrated previously in Rempel (2012). The most successful simulations produce extended penumbrae using a potential magnetic field top boundary, in contrast to previous simulations of extended penumbra with an artificial enhancement of horizontal magnetic field at the top boundary.

background.title: Stability of crystalline measures under random perturbations
background.abstract: In this paper, we study random perturbations and the diffraction properties of translation-bounded crystalline measures. Under a non-vanishing assumption on the known perturbation factor, we prove that, almost surely, any realization of the perturbed measure preserves sufficient structural information to allow the full recovery of the original measure. Previous works have only considered crystalline measures with uniformly discrete supports and equal-mass atoms. Our general setting includes many important crystalline measures that were excluded until now. To treat this broader setting, we adopt a different framework. In this work, we model the perturbation as a random measure rather than as a random set. In particular, this leads us to consider not only perturbations of the support, but also perturbations of the atoms' masses. On the other hand, using elementary techniques of Fourier analysis, we prove that any translation-bounded crystalline measure has a diffraction measure, and we explicitly compute its diffraction.

background.title: Experimental characterization of magnetic multipole fields up to octupole order using smartphone magnetometry
background.abstract: The multipole expansion is one of the organising ideas of electromagnetism: far from a localised source the field is dominated by its lowest non-vanishing moment, and each successive order decays one power of the distance faster. Although the dipole field is routinely measured in introductory laboratories, higher orders are seldom explored experimentally, because the fields are weak, decay very rapidly and require careful positioning. Here we show that with four identical neodymium cube magnets, a sheet of graph paper and the magnetometer of a smartphone, first-year students can build and characterise not one but three distinct magnetic octupoles (linear, planar and `square' arrangements), together with the dipole and the two quadrupoles that serve as reference. A simple notation and a compact set of formulae, based on the spatial Cartesian moments $M_{pq}=\sum_k m_k x_k^p z_k^q$ of the array, predict which field component survives at each measuring position and how it decays. The measured exponents are $n\simeq 3$, $4$ and $5$ for dipole, quadrupole and octupole arrangements, and the measured prefactors show fair quantitative consistency with the independently determined dipole moment of the magnets once nominal geometry and spacer effects are taken into account. We discuss the systematic effects that limit the octupole measurements (higher-order terms at short distance, residual lower-order moments at long distance, the location of the sensor inside the phone) and the ways in which the activity can be extended. The experiment generalises and unifies previous smartphone-based measurements of dipoles, linear quadrupoles and a linear octupole.

background.title: Superstars, quantum wormholes and von Neumann algebras
background.abstract: We entangle heavy 1/2-BPS states in two copies of $\mathcal{N}=4$ SU($N$) Super-Yang-Mills (SYM) theory. Each copy is separately dual to an extremal, supersymmetric, singular black hole geometry, in which the horizon coincides with a singularity. General ideas in the AdS/CFT correspondence suggest that the entanglement between the two copies should lead to some form of connectivity between the two geometries---a kind of wormhole. We use von Neumann algebra methods in the SYM theory to diagnose the possible existence of such wormholes.

background.title: Sasakian Hodge Numbers of Calabi-Yau Links
background.abstract: The link of an isolated weighted homogeneous hypersurface singularity whose degree equals the sum of its weights is a Sasakian manifold that admits a contact Calabi-Yau structure, and its Sasakian Hodge numbers are dimensions of graded pieces of the Milnor algebra of the defining polynomial. In earlier work these numbers were computed with Gröbner bases for the $7$-dimensional links of $7549$ of the $7555$ weighted Calabi-Yau threefold links, and two conjectures were raised from the data. The first asserts that polynomials with the same weights have Milnor algebras whose relevant graded pieces have equal dimensions; the second asserts that the Sasakian Hodge number $h^{2,1}_S$ of the link is bounded above by the Hodge number $h^{2,1}$ of the base Calabi-Yau threefold. Both conjectures are proved here. The first holds for every polynomial with an isolated singularity, because its partial derivatives form a regular sequence; an independent derivation of the Sasakian Hodge numbers by sheaf cohomology on the leaf-space orbifold is also given. For the second, the stringy Hodge numbers of the Calabi-Yau orbifold are shown to bound the middle Sasakian Hodge numbers in every dimension $n\ge2$, and for $n\ge3$ the gap in $h^{n-1,1}$ is shown to be a sum of geometric genera of loci of orbifold points; for threefolds the bound is attained exactly when all curves of orbifold points are rational. The resulting closed formulae give the Sasakian Hodge numbers of the six $7$-dimensional links left open in the earlier work and complete datasets for all $95$ five-dimensional K3 links and all $1\,100\,055$ nine-dimensional Calabi-Yau fourfold links; for the K3 links they recover the previously known second Betti numbers.

background.title: Polynomial integrals and Poisson structures of the Pais-Uhlenbeck oscillator
background.abstract: We classify the autonomous polynomial integrals of the nondegenerate fourth-order Pais-Uhlenbeck oscillator. For a rational frequency ratio $m:n$ in lowest terms, the two sector energies together with the real and imaginary parts of a single ladder product generate all polynomial integrals, subject to one defining relation. The smallest total degree of an integral not expressible through the sector energies is $m+n$, and this bound is attained. For an irrational ratio only polynomials in the sector energies are conserved. In normal-mode variables the commensurate case is the negative oscillator resonance, and the classification realizes its invariant theory in the original higher-derivative variables. Two compatible Poisson structures generate the same dynamics with an indefinite and a positive-definite Hamiltonian. They induce different brackets on the same physical generators. We show that diagonal rescalings of the generators identifying the two abstract Poisson algebras exist only when $m$ or $n$ is even, and that none of them preserves the physical domain of nonnegative sector energies. Finally, we express the generators in terms of the original coordinate and its first three derivatives. The classical multiplier identity gives their variational characteristics in closed form and shows that the additional resonant integrals cannot arise from point variational symmetries.

background.title: ADfiRe: An empirical- and CFD-informed advection-diffusion-reaction thermal model for wildfire spread
background.abstract: Real-time wildfire forecasting requires a trade-off between rapid yet physically relevant models and high fidelity but computationally costly models of flame spread over heterogeneous, multiphase solid fuel. The present study introduces ADfiRe, a hybrid framework that integrates empirical correlations and CFD-informed parameterizations into a physics-based advection-diffusion-reaction (ADR) formulation. The key features of ADfiRe are the use of established fuel databases, the capacity to handle multiple fuels, and a methodology to capture the effect of arbitrary topography. Furthermore, it includes the effect of flame tilting due to wind, thus accounting for the differences between plume- and wind-dominated fire propagation. ADfiRe resolves explicitly the coupled thermochemical degradation as well as heat and mass transport mechanisms of the advancing fire front. The wind field is modeled based on an appropriately defined Byram number. The model is validated against five well-documented experimental field-scale fires in Mediterranean shrublands, showing quantitative agreement with key metrics such as the rate of spread (ROS) and the fireline intensity, through a two-stage, Arrhenius-based heterogeneous reaction scheme coupling solid-fuel pyrolysis and oxygen-limited char/volatile combustion.

background.title: Methanol substitution suppresses deflagration-excited knock and increases the efficiency of a hydrogen-fuelled CFR engine
background.abstract: Knock restricts the performance of hydrogen spark-ignition engines and is usually attributed to end-gas autoignition. To the authors' knowledge, this is the first study in which methanol is used to replace part of the hydrogen in a hydrogen engine at constant fuel energy addition, and it shows that near the knock boundary the limiting oscillation is excited by the deflagration itself, which methanol removes without derating the performance. Port-injected methanol replaced 20--50% of the hydrogen energy in a variable-compression Cooperative Fuel Research engine at 600 rpm and compression ratios of 8--12. With pure hydrogen, oscillation in the 4--15 kHz range began before 10% of the charge had burned in 97--100% of cycles, and its maximum amplitude (MAPO) followed the maximum pressure-rise rate across 2499 cycles (Spearman $ρ=0.94$). Methanol slowed the deflagration: it replaced high-flame-speed hydrogen, cooled the intake by 24--25 K and, at unchanged intake pressure, enleaned the mixture by 10--13%. At 50% methanol, the 10--90% combustion duration lengthened 2.7--3.0-fold, oscillation onset moved 4.5--8.3$^\circ$CA after CA10 and mean MAPO fell by 89--93% although the spark timing was advanced by 13--19$^\circ$CA, and IMEP and indicated thermal efficiency rose by 2.4--7.8%. Methanol was thus worth more than this advance, and at matched CA50 MAPO was still about 90% lower. The measured combustion duration of all 25 data sets scaled with the computed laminar flame speed as $S_L^{-0.58}$ ($R^2=0.99$); fuel replacement accounted for about three quarters of the reduction in $S_L$, and the end-gas autoignition integral stayed below 0.07, against 1 at autoignition. The chamber kept its cylindrical acoustic modes, whose frequencies fell by 8--9%. The trade-off is formaldehyde emissions, which rose five- to sixfold while NO$_x$ fell by 49--85%.

background.title: The BCC Lattice Maximizes the First Positive Neumann Eigenvalue among 3D Lattice Voronoi Cells
background.abstract: It is shown that, among three-dimensional lattices of fixed covolume, the body-centered cubic lattice maximizes the first positive Neumann eigenvalue of its Voronoi cell uniquely, up to orthogonal transformations.

background.title: Group classification of a class of generalized Korteweg-de Vries equations
background.abstract: Applying the method of furcate splitting, we carry out the complete group classification of a class of generalized Korteweg-de Vries equations. This class includes the Korteweg-de Vries, modified Korteweg-de Vries and Harry Dym equations, as well as the Rosenau-Hyman compacton equations. The equivalence group of the class is computed in two independent ways, by the advanced version of the direct method and by the megaideal-based version of the algebraic method. As a by-product, we construct the automorphism group of the equivalence algebra and all its megaideals, whose number is infinite. We also find all additional point equivalences between the classification cases. The maximal Lie invariance algebras of equations from the class are of dimensions from two to five, and all the corresponding Lie-symmetry extensions are regular except those for the equations similar to the Harry Dym equation, which are singular and are the only ones of the maximal dimension five. Finally, we classify the conservation laws of equations from the class with characteristics of nonpositive order.

background.title: Soft Excess Variability and a Test of X-ray Reprocessing in AGN Mrk 359 and NGC 4051 using NICER and TESS
background.abstract: Continuum reverberation mapping of AGN accretion disks assumes that X-ray reprocessing drives the UV/optical variations on short timescales. This reprocessing should also produce an X-ray reflection spectrum, which could be the soft excess observed in many Type 1 AGN. Consequently, if the soft excess traces the reflected emission, the soft excess and optical light curves should be correlated because their variability is driven by the same illuminating X-ray continuum. We present results from a cross-correlation study using simultaneous NICER and TESS observations of $\sim$$30\mathrm{~days}$ for two AGN: Mrk 359 and NGC 4051. We performed time-resolved spectroscopic fits to the X-ray data using a model with power-law and soft-excess components. We find no strong correlation between the optical and soft excess light curves, with correlation coefficients $R(τ)$ $\sim$0.5 for both sources. The total X-ray light curve also shows a similarly poor correlation with the optical variations. However, we find a stronger correlation between the primary X-ray flux and the soft excess flux for both sources. The lack of correlation between the primary X-rays and soft-excess with the optical variations implies that simple linear X-ray reprocessing is not the dominant process driving the optical variability. Either an intervening reprocessor between the inner X-ray region and outer disc is present that dilutes the X-ray-optical correlation, or the optical variability is driven by other mechanisms such as extreme-UV reprocessing or intrinsic disk variability.

background.title: delta-Derivations of Finite-Dimensional Simple Lie Algebras with Values in Arbitrary Modules
background.abstract: We determine the spaces of \(δ\)-derivations of finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebras with values in arbitrary modules for \(δ\ne0,1\). In rank at least two, these derivations vanish unless \(δ=\frac{1}{2}\), in which case they are precisely the module homomorphisms from the adjoint module. For \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\), we characterize the derivation spaces in terms of Casimir eigenspaces and determine when they are nonzero. When the coefficient module is simple, every nonzero derivation module is simple except possibly at \(δ=2\), where it has a simple essential socle with a finite-dimensional semisimple quotient. We describe these modules via translation functors and give explicit formulas for the derivations.

background.title: Annihilation versus anchoring of a topologically charged pair on a perforated two-dimensional surface
background.abstract: Two independent random walks of opposite topological charge move on the discrete torus $(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^2$, which contains $k$ well-separated holes. The walks annihilate when they come within a core distance of each other, and each walk is anchored when it first touches a hole. We prove that the probability of annihilation before anchoring converges to $w_0/(w_0+\sum_j w_j)$, where the weights are explicit and depend only logarithmically on the sizes of the core and of the holes; for point-like core and holes, the limit is $1/(1+k)$. We then prove a fate theorem: the pair either terminates or ends as two opposite charges anchored on two different holes, with probability $(k-1)/(k+1)$ in the point-like case, and the hosting pair $\{j,l\}$ is chosen with probability proportional to $w_jw_l$. The proof combines an abstract competition lemma for rare sets in reversible Markov chains with sharp two-dimensional Green's function estimates.
